translation_en: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Thawr informed me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I was always eager to ask ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab about the two wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning whom Allah Most High said, ‘If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…’ (66:4). I could not ask him until he went for Hajj and I went with him. On the way, he turned aside with a water skin to relieve himself. When he came back, I poured water over his hands from it and he performed ablution. I said to him, ‘Commander of the Faithful, who were the two wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning whom Allah Most High said, “If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…”’ He said, ‘How astonishing, Ibn ‘Abbas! They were ‘A’ishah and Hafsah.’ Then ‘Umar continued the account: ‘I and a neighbor of mine from the Ansar lived among Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, in the upper part of Madinah. We used to take turns visiting the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He would go one day, and I would go the next. When I went, I brought him news of what had happened that day, whether revelation or something else; when my neighbor went, he did the same. We, the Quraysh, used to prevail over our women. When we came among the Ansar, we found a people whose women prevailed over them. Our women began adopting the ways of the Ansari women. I spoke harshly to my wife, but she answered me back, and I objected to her answering me. She said, “Why do you object to my answering you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, answer him back, and one of them may shun him from morning until night.” That alarmed me, and I said to her, “The one among them who does that has surely failed.” Then I gathered my clothes and went down to Hafsah. I said to her, “Hafsah, does one of you really make the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, angry from morning until night?” She said, “Yes.” I said, “You have failed and lost. Do you feel safe from Allah becoming angry because His Messenger is angry with you, and thereby being ruined? Do not demand too much from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, do not answer him back about anything, and do not shun him. Ask me whatever you wish. Do not be deceived because your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him”—meaning ‘A’ishah. ‘Umar said: We had been talking about how Ghassan was preparing horses for our expedition. On my neighbor’s appointed day, he went to visit the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and returned to us in the evening. He pounded hard on my door and said, “Is he there?” I was alarmed and went out to him. He said, “Something tremendous happened today.” I asked, “What is it? Has Ghassan come?” He said, “No, something greater and more alarming: the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has divorced his wives.” I said, “Hafsah has failed and lost! I thought this was about to happen.” I gathered my clothes and prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He entered an upper room of his and secluded himself there. I went to Hafsah and found her weeping. I said, “What makes you weep? Had I not warned you about this? Has the Prophet divorced you?” She said, “I do not know. Here he is, secluded in the upper room.” I went out and came to the pulpit, where I found a group of people around it, some of them weeping. I sat with them for a little while, but what I was feeling overcame me. I went to the upper room where the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was and said to a black servant of his, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” The servant went in, spoke to the Prophet, and returned. He said, “I mentioned you to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he was silent.” I went back and sat with the group by the pulpit. Then what I was feeling overcame me again, so I went and said to the servant, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” He went in and returned, saying, “I mentioned you to him, and he was silent.” I went back and sat with the group by the pulpit. Then what I was feeling overcame me again, so I went to the servant and said, “Ask permission for ‘Umar.” He went in and returned to me, saying, “He was silent when I mentioned you.” As I turned to leave, the servant called me and said, “The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, has given you permission.” I entered to see the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and found him lying on a mat of woven palm leaves, with no bedding between him and it; the mat had left marks on his side. He was leaning on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fiber. I greeted him and, while standing, said, “Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?” He looked up at me and said, “No.” I said, “Allah is greatest!” Then, still standing to put him at ease, I said, “Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me! We Quraysh used to prevail over our women, but when we came to Madinah we found a people whose women prevail over them.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, smiled. Then I said, “Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me when I went to Hafsah and said, ‘Do not be deceived because your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet’”—meaning ‘A’ishah. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, smiled again. When I saw him smile, I sat down. I looked around his home and, by Allah, I saw nothing that caught the eye except three hides. I said, “Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to grant your community abundance. The Persians and Romans have been given abundance and worldly goods, although they do not worship Allah.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sat up; he had been reclining. He said, “Is that what concerns you, Ibn al-Khattab? Those people have been given their good things sooner in the life of this world.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to forgive me.” The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, stayed apart from his wives for 29 nights because of that matter, after Hafsah had disclosed it to ‘A’ishah. He had said, “I will not go in to them for a month,” because he was so angry with them after Allah had reproached him. When 29 nights had passed, he went in to ‘A’ishah first. ‘A’ishah said to him, “Messenger of Allah, you swore that you would not come in to us for a month, but I have counted only 29 nights since you began.” He said, “A month is 29 days.” That month was indeed 29 nights. ‘A’ishah said: Then Allah Most High revealed the verse giving the Prophet’s wives a choice. He began with me, the first of his wives, and I chose him. Then he gave all his wives the choice, and they each said what ‘A’ishah had said.
